advances: Intrinsic effective-section measure with per-fiber Hausdorff dimension $d-1$. Its overlap bounds concern these sections and supply no ambient shape derivative or ambient mixed-volume cap budget.

proof:
The affine coordinates $(z,t)\mapsto(z,y+t-vzu)$ for $t\in u^\perp$ preserve the $(d-1)$-volume within each integer fiber. For $d=1$ the measure in these coordinates has the three atomic weights $(s,1,s)$ with $s\le1$, and the two through-zero half-lines show that the exact depth is $1+s$ in raw mass units.

Let $d\ge2$ and denote the central section in $t$ by $L$, a full-dimensional convex body in $u^\perp$. The two endpoint measures $\alpha,\chi$ are dominated by ordinary $(d-1)$-volume on their compact convex sections, whose midpoint set is contained in $L$. Their first moments and the uniform first moment of $L$ sum to zero after the affine change of coordinates, by the assumed moment identity and equality of the endpoint masses. For $s=0$, zero is the ordinary centroid of $L$ and 6769574fc1bd9f8d with selected mass $|L|$ gives the stronger ordinary bound on every nonconstant halfspace trace at the central base. A pure-base halfspace includes all of $L$.

For $s>0$, use the midpoint displacement coupling in the proof of dfd25e72c1f45a4e in dimension $d-1$ on the normalized compactly supported densities $\alpha/s,\chi/s$. Their $L^\infty$ bounds are at most $1/s$, so the coupling's midpoint law multiplied by $s$ is a measure $\eta\le\mathbf 1_L dt$ of mass $s$. Its first moment is half the sum of the endpoint first moments. Thus zero is the centroid of $\mathbf 1_L dt+2\eta$, and $s\le |L|=S_0$. If a containing halfspace of the cap plane has nonconstant trace on the middle section's affine space, a midpoint in the halfspace forces at least one coupled endpoint into the same closed halfspace. The captured mass is at least $|L\cap J_0|+\eta(J_0)$ for its middle trace $J_0$. By 607dca34de472b94 this is at least $3\Gamma_{d-1}(|L|+s)/4$, which is at least $\Gamma_{d-1}(|L|+2s)/2$ because $s\le |L|$. A pure-base halfspace takes the central section and at least one endpoint, so has at least half the total. This proves the depth claim in all cases.

Each of the two closed sides of $H'$ contains the anchor; on the plane their measures sum to $S+\tau(\partial H')$. If a side is the whole plane it also satisfies the lower bound. This proves the two-sided inequality. For nonparallel continuous normals, the common plane cuts a set of zero $H^{d-1}$-measure inside each section, so $b'=0$. For parallel normals the $H'$ margin on the section is exactly $(v'-\epsilon v)z$. A zero coefficient gives $p=b'=1$; a nonzero coefficient gives the entire central section and exactly one endpoint, with boundary containing the central section only. We proved $s\le S_0$ by midpoint domination for $d\ge2$, and it follows from the atomic bound for $d=1$, giving the lower value $2/3$. Finally the own cap contains the whole section and each other cap pays at least $\kappa S$. Summing these inequalities with weights $\lambda$ gives the stated mixture estimate.

statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and let convex bodies $K_{-1},K_0,K_1\subset\mathbb R^d$ at the indicated bases satisfy $(K_{-1}+K_1)/2\subseteq K_0$. Fix $y\in\operatorname{int}K_0$, a unit vector $u$, and $v\in\mathbb R$. In the ambient plane $P=\{u\cdot(x-y)+vz=0\}$ let $\tau$ be the sum of the ordinary central section measure and endpoint submeasures dominated by the respective $H^{d-1}$ section measures. Assume the endpoint masses are both $s\ge0$ and $\int x\,d\tau=S y$, where $S=S_0+2s$ is the total and $S_0>0$ is the central section mass. Write $\Gamma_q=(q/(q+1))^q$ for $q\ge1$ and $\Gamma_0=1$. Every closed halfspace of $P$ containing $(0,y)$ has $\tau$-mass at least $\kappa S$, where $\kappa=\Gamma_{d-1}/2$. If $d\ge2$ and $s=0$, the lower bound improves to $\Gamma_{d-1}S$. If $d=1$, the exact depth fraction is $(1+s)/(1+2s)$.

For any closed ambient through-$(0,y)$ cap $H'=\{u'\cdot(x-y)+v'z\ge0\}$ with unit $u'$, set $p=\tau(H')/S$ and $b'=\tau(\partial H')/S$. Then $\kappa\le p\le\min(1,1-\kappa+b')$. If $u'$ and $u$ are nonparallel, $b'=0$. If $u'=\epsilon u$, $\epsilon\in\{-1,1\}$, and $v'=\epsilon v$, then $p=b'=1$. Otherwise in the parallel case
$$
p=\frac{S_0+s}{S_0+2s}\in[2/3,1],\qquad b'=\frac{S_0}{S_0+2s}.
$$
In a finite family of such anchored caps, the average cap indicator on any one's effective section is at least $\kappa+(1-\kappa)\lambda_j$ in normalized section mass, where $\lambda_j$ is that section's own cap weight in the probability mixture.
title: Depth and intersections of balanced effective cap sections
